title: Two weeks of longer sleep at home: what 80 adults then ate [baseline_and_intervention_periods, overall_mean_age]
teaser: The trial took 80 adults with overweight who slept under 6.5 hours a night. [overall_mean_age, eligibility_age_bmi_sleep] Sleep advice gave the sleep group 1.2 hours more sleep a night than the control group. [sleep_duration_diff] Over 2 weeks they ate 270.4 kcal a day less than the control group, with no diet. [baseline_and_intervention_periods, ei_diff_in_changes, free_living_routine] Part of that gap came from the control group eating more than before. [ei_ctrl_change, limit_control_increase]
hook: This trial gave 80 adults no diet and no exercise plan. [overall_mean_age, free_living_routine] It aimed to change one thing, their time in bed, and then measured what they ate. [sleep_extension_target, energy_intake_method]
populationPanel: Who was studied: 80 adults aged 21 to 40 with overweight (a BMI of 25.0 to 29.9). [overall_mean_age, eligibility_age_bmi_sleep] They usually slept less than 6.5 hours a night. [eligibility_age_bmi_sleep] Chance put each of them into longer sleep or their usual schedule, for 2 weeks at home. [randomization_method, baseline_and_intervention_periods, free_living_routine] People with sleep apnea, insomnia or recent shift work could not take part. [exclusion_sleep_disorders_shift]

card.question: Do adults eat less when they sleep longer at home? [sleep_extension_target, ei_diff_in_changes]
card.headline: Compared with the control group, adults who slept longer ate 270.4 kcal a day less. [ei_diff_in_changes]
card.support: The energy adults burned showed no clear difference between the groups. [tee_diff_in_changes, tee_p_value]

paragraphs: Think of your weight as a ledger with two columns. [-] Food goes into one column. [-] The energy people burn, at rest and on the move, goes into the other. [energy_intake_method]

Short sleep tips that ledger. [prior_lab_sleep_restriction_range] In laboratory studies, people whose sleep was cut ate about 250 to 350 kcal a day more, and burned about the same. [prior_lab_sleep_restriction_range]

This trial asked the question the other way round, at home. [free_living_routine] Adults who extended their sleep ate less, while the energy they burned showed no clear difference. [ei_ext_change, tee_diff_in_changes] Each extra hour of sleep went with about 162 kcal a day less food. [energy_intake_per_hour_sleep]

With less coming in and no clear change going out, the ledger moved the other way. [eb_diff_in_changes] Over 2 weeks, the sleep group lost 0.48 kg, while the control group gained 0.39 kg. [baseline_and_intervention_periods, wt_ext_change, wt_ctrl_change]

figure.caption: Change from each group’s usual 2 weeks, as the paper measured it. [baseline_and_intervention_periods]
figure.alt: Two groups of adults, one above the other, each with a bar for food eaten and a bar for energy burned. [energy_intake_method, dlw_method] In the longer-sleep group, the food bar falls below no change and the energy-burned bar dips much less. [ei_ext_change, tee_ext_change] In the usual-sleep group, the food bar rises and the energy-burned bar barely moves. [ei_ctrl_change, tee_ctrl_change] Under each group sits its change in weight. [wt_ext_change, wt_ctrl_change]

params.title: Food in, energy out
params.unit: Change from each group’s usual weeks, kcal a day

paragraphs: For 2 weeks, everyone kept their usual sleep at home. [baseline_and_intervention_periods] Then chance split them into 2 groups for 2 more weeks. [randomization_method, baseline_and_intervention_periods] The sleep group had a personal sleep advice session, aiming for 8.5 hours in bed each night. [sleep_hygiene_counseling_delivery, sleep_extension_target]

Nobody got a diet or an exercise plan. [free_living_routine] A wrist sensor recorded sleep for all 4 weeks. [sleep_monitoring_duration, actigraphy_device] A home scale they could not read weighed them twice every morning. [hidden_scale_weights] Researchers measured the energy participants burned, and worked out food eaten from that plus changes in body stores. [dlw_method, energy_intake_method, body_energy_stores_method]

audit.effect: Change in daily energy intake, sleep group against control: 270.4 kcal a day lower (P < .001). [ei_diff_in_changes, ei_p_value]
audit.weakEnd: The 95% confidence interval runs from 393.4 to 147.4 kcal a day lower. [ei_diff_in_changes] Even at the weak end, the sleep group ate 147.4 kcal a day less. [ei_diff_in_changes]
limitations: The control group’s rise in intake and weight may have added to the gap. [limit_control_increase]
The change lasted 2 weeks, so nobody knows how long people keep the longer nights. [baseline_and_intervention_periods, limit_short_duration_sustainability]
The method that measured the energy participants burned is precise to about 5%, which adds uncertainty to each intake figure. [limit_dlw_precision]
Only adults with overweight who met strict rules took part, so the result may not hold for others. [limit_generalizability]
audit.missed: Both groups moved: intake fell by 155.5 kcal a day in the sleep group and rose by 114.9 in the control group. [ei_ext_change, ei_ctrl_change] Of the 0.87 kg weight gap, 0.62 kg was fat-free mass and 0.25 kg was fat. [wt_diff_in_changes, ffm_diff_in_changes, fm_diff_in_changes]
more: Total energy participants burned (53.9 kcal a day, P = .19) and energy burned through activity showed no clear difference. [tee_diff_in_changes, tee_p_value, aee_day_p_value]

At rest while fasting, participants in the sleep group burned 32.5 kcal a day less (P = .047); after a meal there was no clear difference (P = .41). [rmr_fast_diff_in_changes, rmr_fast_p_value, rmr_post_p_value]
75 of 80 (93.8%) had complete intake data (sleep group 90.0%, control group 97.5%). [overall_mean_age, complete_ei_data_overall, complete_ei_by_group]
A weight model predicts about 12 kg lost over 3 years if a drop of about 270 kcal a day lasted; the trial did not test that. [hall_model_prediction]
Funded by the US National Institutes of Health; no conflicts of interest reported. [funding_sources, conflict_of_interest]

glossary.plain: Body mass index: weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared, a rough measure of body size.
Kilocalories, the unit of food energy that labels usually just call calories.

takeaways: Aiming for 8.5 hours in bed, adults who had slept under 6.5 hours got 1.2 hours more sleep than the control group. [eligibility_age_bmi_sleep, sleep_extension_target, sleep_duration_diff]
Compared with the control group, they ate 270.4 kcal a day less, with no diet. [ei_diff_in_changes, free_living_routine]
The authors noted that limiting electronic devices seemed to matter to participants; the trial did not test it on its own. [limit_sleep_factors_unassessed]
